This may be an odd question, but I’m hoping someone here may have some experience with this.

I work in Pre-Admission Testing for a privately owned outpatient surgery center (we don’t use epic. )Part of my job is obtaining medical clearances, cardiology clearances, office notes, EKGs, test results, and other records for patients who are scheduled for surgery.

Does anyone know if there is a way for someone in my position to obtain outside access to another health system’s Epic—for example, Prisma Health Epic—to view or pull records for mutual patients?

I don’t work for Prisma, so I’m wondering if they offer something like EpicCare Link or another type of provider access for outside facilities.

topComments.text: We utilize prisma and Epic Carelink. We have 2 hospitals that use EPiC so we PDF the records we need and attach to pt docs.

Yes. You need Epic Care Link access from the hospital in question. This is how we access all the records on our patients from our local Children’s Hospital and from the newborn nurseries at community hospitals that we round at. They are all on Epic. We are on ECW.

items.text: Anybody care to share your incoming referral workflow for when a provider refers someone to your office as a specialist or for a procedure? We're having a tremendously difficult time following the preloaded status and substatus option, especially since we cannot change the date to know when we need to work on the next step since that's a hard coded/locked field.

topComments.text:
We only use the eCW referral module to keep track of referral due dates for patients whose plan requires a referral. 

For referrals from PCPs, we triage them from the fax inbox to a user we created named “new patient referral inbox.” Anyone can go to their d jellybean, select that user, and see all of the incoming referral faxes. We have one staff member who goes through those documents, makes a patient profile with all of the info from the referral, and calls the patient to schedule. If they reach the patient and schedule them, they mark the document reviewed and it falls out of the list. If they don’t reach the pt, they make a note in the document box about when they called, and leave it unreviewed.

What I do is keep the status for the referral stage and track the actual next follow-up separately. For example: referral received → verify insurance/auth → schedule appointment → confirm appointment → close once records/consult are received. This makes it easier for my team to know what needs to be worked next.
